open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: REGISTRY_BASE_URL ownership and validation lifecycle
open_points.text: “Environment values are read once, by `runtime_settings`, into `RuntimeSettings`” but “`registry_gateway` reads `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` at each Registry call”; meanwhile `runtime_settings` owns loading, normalizing and validating the closed environment table once at start, while A6 says the service starts without this value and the gateway decides whether its call-time value is usable.
open_points.question: Which module exclusively owns reading, normalizing and validating `REGISTRY_BASE_URL`: `runtime_settings` at startup or `registry_gateway` at each call, and is any startup-captured value authoritative?
options: `registry_gateway` exclusively reads and validates the live environment value for every call; `runtime_settings` excludes this variable.
`runtime_settings` reads and validates it once into `RuntimeSettings`; the gateway uses that captured value.
`runtime_settings` captures an optional value, but the gateway independently rereads and validates the environment at call time.
open_points.default_guess: Treat `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` as exclusively owned and read live by `registry_gateway`, excluding it from the effective startup settings.

witness.initial: The service starts while `REGISTRY_BASE_URL=https://registry-a` is usable.
events: The host operator changes `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` to `https://registry-b` without restarting the service.
A staff or viewer operation requires Registry validation.
outcomes: `registry_gateway` rereads the environment and calls registry-b.
The operation uses the value loaded into `RuntimeSettings` at startup and calls registry-a.
witness.observer: The Registry operators and the API caller see which Registry is contacted and which project answer controls the operation.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES ownership and validation lifecycle
open_points.text: “`binary_storage` reads `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` at each binary read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable” conflicts with A30’s “`BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` (required positive integer)”, “an invalid or missing required variable stops start-up”, and `runtime_settings` owning startup validation and binary-bound consistency.
open_points.question: Must a missing or invalid `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` stop startup, or may the service start and refuse only binary reads; and which module owns parsing and validating it?
options: It is startup-required and owned by `runtime_settings`; `binary_storage` receives the validated bound.
It is call-time configuration owned by `binary_storage`; missing or invalid values affect only that read.
Both validate it, with an explicit rule for which value and failure takes precedence.
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the changed running behavior: let `binary_storage` own call-time parsing and make the variable non-required at startup.

events: A viewer requests an otherwise-authorized expense document.
outcomes: Startup is refused because a required positive integer is missing; no API caller can reach the service.
Startup succeeds; ordinary API operations work, but the document read is refused when `binary_storage` checks the missing value.
witness.observer: The host operator and the viewer see whether the service starts and whether only the binary request fails.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT ownership and validation lifecycle
open_points.text: “`binary_storage` reads `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` … at each binary read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable” conflicts with R0-10’s statement that the service is configured only by environment variables “which it validates when it starts” and with `runtime_settings` owning the closed environment table’s startup loading and validation.
open_points.question: Is `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` validated and captured by `runtime_settings` at startup, or read and validated exclusively by `binary_storage` for each read?
options: `runtime_settings` owns startup validation and passes a fixed root to `binary_storage`.
`binary_storage` owns live call-time reading and validation; a bad root does not prevent startup.
Startup and call-time validation both occur, with the authoritative value and failure semantics stated explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the changed running behavior: make `binary_storage` the sole owner of live root reading and validation.

witness.initial: The service starts with `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT=/srv/binaries-a`, containing an authorized document.
events: The host changes `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` to `/srv/binaries-b`, where that document is absent, without restarting.
outcomes: `binary_storage` rereads the environment, uses `/srv/binaries-b`, and the document read is refused as unavailable/concealed.
The service uses the root captured by `runtime_settings`, reads `/srv/binaries-a`, and returns the document bytes.
witness.observer: The viewer sees either the document or the read failure; the host sees which storage root is accessed.
